headline: Baidu's Apollo Go will let more than 1,000 Hong Kong residents ride its driverless taxis for free in a two-week public trial starting on 21 Oct 2026.
score_reason: First public robotaxi trial in Hong Kong, but small, short, free and limited to a fixed route.
importance_line: Hong Kong residents get their first public rides in driverless cars, but the trial is short, free and limited to one 5 km route in Tung Chung.
summary: dotdotnews reports that Apollo Go, the self-driving ride-hailing service of Chinese search company Baidu, will run Hong Kong's first public robotaxi trial from 21 Oct to 3 Nov 2026 in Tung Chung, with free rides for more than 1,000 people. Each ride covers about 5.1 km in around 15 minutes, tickets go out through district offices from 16 Oct, and Apollo Go's cars have covered more than 280,000 km in the city under the first pilot licence.
notes: SCMP (the pool source) was blocked; facts read from dotdotnews on the same announcement. The trial has not started yet.
